lines.text: Open in Atlanta, then move straight through New York, Los Angeles and London in the order the team set; put the biggest spend and street-level work into New York first, then Los Angeles, with Atlanta as the launch anchor and London as the leanest stop.
Keep the whole plan inside a micro budget by spending on content, local street teams, one low-cost support ask per city and one small brand trade per market, not on paid media or big production.

Lead Atlanta with Wayne Brady as the support ask, because he is the only opener name returned for this audience and age band in the city and he gives the room a familiar face without a big-fee booking.
Hook the album around R&B made for late nights and replay, with the release framed as a city-to-city run that starts in Atlanta and peaks in New York and Los Angeles before London.
Keep the first message simple: this is an R&B album landing in ten weeks, and the rollout is built to meet 18 to 24 year-olds where they actually move online and in the room.

Make the third message about the sonic lane: keep the press framing around modern R&B that sits near SZA, Summer Walker and Brent Faiyaz, with one extra nod to SZA’s wider lane if the team wants a firmer comp set.
SZA should be used as the closest press shorthand for this launch lane, because it is one of the requested comps and it helps position the album as current, melody-led R&B for younger listeners.
Summer Walker should be used as a close match that signals contemporary, relationship-forward R&B to booking teams and editors who track the current female-led lane.
Brent Faiyaz should be used as the nearest male comp for booking and press, because he signals a smoother, moodier R&B lane that fits late-night programming and club-adjacent rooms.

The core people who like music like yours are 25 to 29, with 18 to 24 next; keep the target audience in the creative, but lead the message with the older slice so the campaign still lands with the broader group that already shows up most strongly.
In Los Angeles, people who like music like yours watch P-Valley, Harlem and Gentefied, which makes the city a strong fit for visual-first creator clips and neighborhood-led discovery.
Atlanta should be the launch anchor: use Old Fourth Ward and Little Five Points for street teams, posters and a listening meet-up, and keep the city’s support ask low-cost and familiar.
New York should carry the heaviest audience spend: hit Harlem and Brooklyn, and pair one campus move with a late-night room or listening event so the release shows up where people already gather.

understanding.asked: The user wants a full launch plan for their upcoming R&B album release within a ten-week window.
goals: Successfully launch the new R&B album Night Songs
Engage fans aged 18 to 24 through a targeted release strategy
constraints: Budget is under ten thousand dollars
Launch timing is in ten weeks
Tour stops must follow the exact order of Atlanta, New York, Los Angeles, and London

readers.who: Young adults and college students who are contemporary R&B enthusiasts
readers.consumes: Releases by SZA, Summer Walker, and Brent Faiyaz, along with mood-driven R&B playlists
readers.why: The artist's musical style and target demographic directly align with the core audience of modern alternative R&B.

criteria.text: Fits within the micro budget of under ten thousand dollars
Aligns with the ten week release window
Follows the exact tour city order of Atlanta, New York, Los Angeles, and London
Reaches fans aged 24 and younger using Qloo taste data
Reflects the sonic profile of SZA, Summer Walker, and Brent Faiyaz

issues.text: The budget is not kept under the stated micro cap: the draft opens with a $10,000 split and repeatedly treats $10,000 as the working budget.
issues.fix: Rework the spend to fit strictly under $10k, with every line item scaled to a sub-$10k total and no language that implies $10k is the available budget.

issues.text: The draft says the team’s route order is Atlanta, New York, Los Angeles and London, but then says the stronger order starts New York, Los Angeles, Atlanta and London as if that should replace the given order.
issues.fix: Keep the user’s exact tour order as the operating plan and, if you mention the alternative, frame it only as a route-strength note that does not override the requested sequence.

issues.text: The draft says the under-24 audience should not be the only focus and repeatedly centers the older 25 to 29 group, but the request is specifically for fans aged 18 to 24. The evidence does show the younger segment is smaller, not that it should be de-prioritized.
issues.fix: Write the plan to reach 18 to 24 directly, using the older audience insight only as a constraint on tone and messaging, not as the target focus.

issues.text: The draft says SZA, Summer Walker and Brent Faiyaz are all close matches and “the clearest press signal,” but the evidence says the artist and its sound-alikes lean on one name for the result, so another sound-alike from your side would firm it up.
issues.fix: Soften the comp language to what the evidence supports and present the trio as the stated reference set, not as fully confirmed equal-strength matches.

issues.text: The budget section says ‘A starting split of $10,000’ even though the request is micro, under about $10k. That reads like the full spend can be $10k rather than staying under it.
issues.fix: Rewrite the budget to keep the total clearly under $10k, or present the split as a cap well below that ceiling and remove wording that makes $10k sound like the planned total.

issues.text: The budget asks to ‘adjust it with your label or booking agent,’ which adds a dependency the request did not include and leaves the micro-budget plan partly unresolved.
issues.fix: Give a self-contained spend plan that works inside the micro budget without needing outside approval to be usable.

issues.text: The timeline starts with ‘T-8’ and other steps that assume an eight-week runway, but the request says the album is out in 10 weeks.
issues.fix: Rebuild the calendar and timeline around a 10-week countdown so every dated step matches the launch window.

issues.text: The audience section says the core audience is older than 18 to 24 and tells the team to keep the copy direct so it still lands with older fans. That shifts away from the requested 18 to 24 focus.
issues.fix: Center the plan on 18 to 24 throughout, and if you mention the broader audience at all, treat it as secondary context rather than the lead target.

issues.text: The plan presents SZA, Summer Walker and Brent Faiyaz as the launch frame, but the evidence says the artist and its sound-alikes lean on one name for the result, so another sound-alike would firm up the read.
issues.fix: Keep the three names as the requested comps, but add the closest missing sonic reference the evidence supports, or soften the claim so it doesn’t sound fully locked.

issues.text: The route section correctly preserves Atlanta, New York, Los Angeles and London in order, but it also says the strongest route is New York, Los Angeles, Atlanta, London. The draft says to use that only as a planning note, yet the main route and spend logic still tilt toward the stronger order without a concrete way to honor the requested sequence throughout.
issues.fix: Keep the tour order fixed in the operating plan and separate any spend prioritization from the run-of-show so the sequence is never treated as optional. Use the requested order as the primary route and make the city-weighting a secondary planning layer.

issues.text: The plan gives a timeline framework, but it does not clearly align the rollout to the stated 10-week release window end-to-end. The calendar and timeline sections conflict on timing, and the plan never cleanly maps all major actions across the ten weeks.
issues.fix: Rewrite the calendar and timeline so they explicitly cover weeks 1 through 10 from now to release, with each major action placed in the correct week and no duplicated or conflicting schedule lines.

issues.text: The Audience section says the core people are 25 to 29 and tells the team to lead with that older slice, even though the request is specifically for fans aged 18 to 24. The evidence says 18 to 24 is smaller, not that it should be deprioritized.
issues.fix: Keep 18 to 24 as the primary target throughout the plan and, if needed, mention 25 to 29 only as a secondary audience without letting it steer the strategy.

issues.text: The comp framing treats SZA, Summer Walker and Brent Faiyaz as fully locked and says the lane is clear, but the evidence says the result leans on one name and would be firmer with another sound-alike. The draft softens this later, but the main positioning still sounds more certain than the evidence supports.
issues.fix: Keep the three requested comps as the launch frame, but explicitly label the sonic read as partial and add a note that one more artist reference from the team would sharpen the comp set.
